summary: City-built 1872 stone light at the north tip of Roosevelt Island (Blackwell's Island) for Hell Gate; a city landmark, now a park.

light.focal_height_note: About 54 ft above the river, fixed red (LighthouseFriends, 1872). The USLHS place record gives 44 ft above water (13.4 m) for its 1904 'Blackwell Island' light; the two may not be the same light.
light.characteristic_note: Fixed red in 1872 per LighthouseFriends; current characteristic not established here.

lens.where: Lantern room; LighthouseFriends says the federal government furnished it. The Historical Society says the federal service furnished lamps.

structures.note: About fifty feet tall; designed by James Renwick, Jr.; stone quarried on the island largely by convict labour. The stone and lantern were restored in later campaigns.

facts.agency: New York City (Department of Parks & Recreation, per LighthouseFriends; managed by New York City, per NPS)

access.note: LighthouseFriends visit note: grounds open, tower closed. Lighthouse Park, northern tip of Roosevelt Island.

facts.register: National Register of Historic Places, listed 16 March 1972 (NPS); New York City landmark, 1975 (LighthouseFriends) or 1976 (RIHS walking tour).

events.note: City of New York purchases the East River island (Blackwell's Island).

Listed on the National Register of Historic Places, 16 March 1972.
Designated a New York City landmark: 1975 per LighthouseFriends; 1976 per the RIHS walking tour. Not resolved.
Partial restoration the year after the landmark designation (LighthouseFriends).
Anonymous donation of $120,000 funds a complete restoration (including internal lamps).

resolved_conflicts.explanation: LighthouseFriends and the RIHS describe a city tower lit in September 1872. The USLHS 'Blackwell Island' record gives a light established in 1904 with a 44 ft focal height and keepers from 1885 to 1895. These may be two different lights (the Blackwells Island Reef light, or a federal lamp on the island) or one record merged with the Hell Gate keepers. Not resolved.
54 ft above the river (LighthouseFriends, 1872) against 44 ft above water (USLHS, 13.4 m). Not resolved.
1975 (LighthouseFriends) against 1976 (RIHS walking tour, which cites a city designation report of 1976 that was not read here). The story gives both.

The USLHS 'Blackwell Island' roster (1885-1895) names men that LighthouseFriends lists as keepers of the Hell Gate (Hallet's Point) light. Not confirmed for the city tower; the rows keep no person link.

notes_for_editor: (1) Identity conflict, the central open question: the sources describe a city-built tower lit in 1872 (LighthouseFriends, the Historical Society, NPS). The USLHS 'Blackwell Island' place (established 1904, 44 ft above water, keepers 1885-1895) matches none of that. LighthouseFriends lists the same keepers for the Hell Gate (Hallet's Point) light, established 1884, about 2,300 ft away. Possibilities: (a) the USLHS record merges the Hell Gate keepers; (b) the 1904 record is the federal Blackwells Island Reef light of the 1917 bulletin; (c) a federal lamp later sat on the city tower. Suggested check: the Light-House Board reports 1885-1905 for any federal Blackwell's Island light, and the NARA keeper registers. (2) Keepers: the 11 roster rows are kept with a note and no person slug; the story names none of them as keepers of the tower. (3) NRHP nomination 72000876 is not digitised at the NPS PDF address (a placeholder); not read. The NPS page says the lighthouse was also documented by the Historic American Buildings Survey; HABS was not read (loc.gov is restricted to the newspaper tool). (4) Landmark year 1975 (LighthouseFriends) vs 1976 (walking tour). The $3.1 million restoration's year is not given in any source read. (5) Newspapers: a Chronicling America search for 1872-1900 returned only generic page hits, and a targeted 1872-1874 search produced no readable output before the run ended; no press account was read, so the story has no newspaper evidence for the 1872 lighting. (6) Focal height: 54 ft (LighthouseFriends) vs 44 ft (USLHS); the station record's 15.0 m tower height matches the RIHS and LighthouseFriends '50 ft'. (7) The coordinates in the station record agree with LighthouseFriends; the USLHS coordinates (about 3.9 km away) were not used. (8) The 1894 Board report quotation is the clean 1894 text; the 1891 text is OCR-damaged and is cited without quotation. (9) No photos proposed. (10) Fact-check 2026-10-22: the story runs to about 920 words with five chapters (The place, Building the light, The keepers, After the keepers, Today), one more than the moderate-evidence shape allows; each chapter has sourced content, so none was merged. (11) The 1894 Board passage is quoted from the 1894 report (scan p.323); the 1891 report repeats the 1883 recommendation, which the story says. The 'Blackwells Island Reef' light is listed separately in the 1917 Bulletin and Commissioner report; whether the USLHS 1904 record describes it is not settled.
